definitions.meaning: To approach, come to, address, greet, welcome

quotations.old_english: Wíf sceal eodor æþelinga [MS. e] ǽrest gegrétan
quotations.english: the wife shall the nobles' chief first greet
he addressed his faithful friend in powerful words

quotations.old_english: Ðæt we mágon úre frýnd geseón and úre siblingas gegrétan
quotations.english: that we may see our friends and greet our kinsmen

quotations.old_english: Man tǽleþ and mid yfle gegréteþ ða ðe riht lufiaþ
quotations.english: men blame and insult those that love right

source_text: ge-grétan; he -grét, pl. -grétaþ; p. -grétte, pl. -grétton; pp. -gréted To approach, come to, address, greet, welcome; adire, alloqui, salutare :-- Wíf sceal eodor æþelinga [MS. e] ǽrest gegrétan the wife shall the nobles' chief first greet, Exon. 90 a; Th. 339, 7; Gn. Ex. 90. Holdne gegrétte meaglum wordum he addressed his faithful friend in powerful words, Beo. Th, 3964; B. 1980. Hie ðá gegrétte he then addressed them, Andr. Kmbl. 507; An. 254. Ðæt we mágon úre frýnd geseón and úre siblingas gegrétan that we may see our friends and greet our kinsmen, Homl. Th. ii. 526, 33. Man tǽleþ and mid yfle gegréteþ ða ðe riht lufiaþ men blame and insult those that love right, Swt. A. S. Rdr. 110, 164. v. grétan.
